rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track;

SELECT ar.ArtistId, ar.Name, COUNT(al.AlbumId) AS AlbumCount FROM Artist ar JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name HAVING COUNT(al.AlbumId) = (SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM Album GROUP BY ArtistId))
rows.note: Assuming "most albums" means the count of rows in Album per artist, with ties included.

rows.sql: SELECT Country, COUNT(*) AS CustomerCount FROM Customer GROUP BY Country ORDER BY CustomerCount DESC, Country;
rows.note: Assuming customers with a NULL country should be grouped together as their own row, I'll count all customers by their Country value.

rows.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS Year, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS TotalRevenue FROM Invoice GROUP BY Year ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: Assuming total revenue is the sum of Invoice.Total grouped by calendar year of InvoiceDate.

rows.sql: SELECT c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS FullName, ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) AS TotalSpent FROM Customer c JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId, c.FirstName, c.LastName ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC LIMIT 5
rows.note: Assumption: total spent is the sum of Invoice.Total per customer, and full name is FirstName plus LastName.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, COUNT(c.CustomerId) AS CustomerCount FROM Customer c JOIN Employee e ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName, e.LastName HAVING COUNT(c.CustomerId) = (SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Customer WHERE SupportRepId IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SupportRepId))
rows.note: Assumption: "support rep" means an Employee referenced by Customer.SupportRepId, and I'll return all tied employees if there's a tie.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(pt.TrackId) AS TrackCount FROM Playlist p JOIN PlaylistTrack pt ON pt.PlaylistId = p.PlaylistId WHERE p.Name = 'Grunge';
SELECT COUNT(*) AS never_purchased_tracks FROM Track t WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM InvoiceLine il WHERE il.TrackId = t.TrackId);
rows.note: Assuming "purchased" means the track appears in any InvoiceLine, I'll count tracks with no matching invoice line.

rows.sql: SELECT BillingCountry, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS Revenue FROM Invoice WHERE InvoiceDate >= '2012-01-01' AND InvoiceDate < '2013-01-01' GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assumption: revenue means the sum of Invoice.Total grouped by BillingCountry for invoices dated in 2012, and I'll return only the top country.

rows.sql: SELECT ar.Name FROM Artist ar JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId WHERE t.GenreId IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 3;
rows.note: Assumption: "tracks in more than 3 genres" means count of distinct GenreId across the artist's tracks (via Album → Artist) is greater than 3.

rows.sql:
SELECT g.Name AS Genre,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) / (SELECT SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity) FROM InvoiceLine), 2) AS Percentage
FROM InvoiceLine il
JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
LEFT JOIN Genre g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
GROUP BY g.Name
ORDER BY Percentage DESC;
rows.note: I'll compute each genre's share of revenue from invoice lines (UnitPrice × Quantity), with percentages relative to the overall total.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT i.CustomerId) AS customer_count
FROM Invoice i
JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
WHERE g.Name = 'Rock'
AND i.CustomerId NOT IN (
  SELECT i2.CustomerId
  FROM Invoice i2
  JOIN InvoiceLine il2 ON il2.InvoiceId = i2.InvoiceId
  JOIN Track t2 ON t2.TrackId = il2.TrackId
  JOIN Genre g2 ON g2.GenreId = t2.GenreId
  WHERE g2.Name = 'Jazz'
);
rows.note: Assumption: a customer "bought" a track if it appears in an InvoiceLine linked to one of their invoices, and genre is matched by Genre.Name.

rows.sql: SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS month, SUM(Total) AS revenue FROM Invoice WHERE strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2011' GROUP BY month ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assumption: revenue is the sum of Invoice.Total for invoices dated in 2011, grouped by calendar month.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM Employee e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Customer c WHERE c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId);
rows.note: Assumption: "no customers assigned" means no Customer row has that employee as SupportRepId, and full name is FirstName plus LastName.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_first_purchase_2010 FROM (SELECT CustomerId, MIN(InvoiceDate) AS first_date FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId) WHERE first_date >= '2010-01-01' AND first_date < '2011-01-01'
rows.note: Assumption: a customer's first purchase is their earliest invoice date, and I count customers whose earliest invoice falls in 2010.

rows.sql: SELECT a.Title, ROUND(SUM(t.Milliseconds) / 60000.0, 1) AS Minutes FROM Album a JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = a.AlbumId GROUP BY a.AlbumId, a.Title ORDER BY SUM(t.Milliseconds) DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assumption: total running time is the sum of Track.Milliseconds per album, converted to minutes (ms / 60000).

rows.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS Year, SUM(Total) AS Revenue
  FROM Invoice
  GROUP BY Year
)
SELECT Year,
       Revenue,
       ROUND((Revenue - LAG(Revenue) OVER (ORDER BY Year)) * 100.0 / LAG(Revenue) OVER (ORDER BY Year), 1) AS YoYPctChange
FROM yearly
ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: I'm assuming revenue means the sum of `Invoice.Total` grouped by calendar year of `InvoiceDate`.

rows.sql:
WITH spend AS (
  SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Total) AS total_spend
  FROM Invoice
  GROUP BY CustomerId
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_above_average
FROM spend
WHERE total_spend > (SELECT AVG(total_spend) FROM spend);
rows.note: Assumption: "total spend" per customer is the sum of Invoice.Total over all their invoices, and the average is taken across customers who have invoices.

rows.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT p.Name AS PlaylistName, COUNT(DISTINCT al.ArtistId) AS ArtistCount
  FROM Playlist p
  JOIN PlaylistTrack pt ON pt.PlaylistId = p.PlaylistId
  JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = pt.TrackId
  JOIN Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
  GROUP BY p.PlaylistId, p.Name
)
SELECT PlaylistName, ArtistCount
FROM counts
WHERE ArtistCount = (SELECT MAX(ArtistCount) FROM counts);
SELECT COUNT(*) AS invoice_count FROM (SELECT il.InvoiceId FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId GROUP BY il.InvoiceId HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 1) AS x
rows.note: Assuming an invoice counts if its InvoiceLine rows reference tracks with at least two distinct GenreId values.

rows.sql:
WITH rep_rev AS (
  SELECT e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS RepName, SUM(i.Total) AS Revenue
  FROM Invoice i
  JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
  JOIN Employee e ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId
  WHERE strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) = '2010'
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, RepName
)
SELECT RepName, ROUND(Revenue, 2) AS Revenue
FROM rep_rev
WHERE Revenue = (SELECT MAX(Revenue) FROM rep_rev);
rows.note: Assumption: "revenue" means the sum of `Invoice.Total` for 2010 invoices, attributed to the support rep assigned to each invoice's customer.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS discontinued_products FROM Products WHERE Discontinued = '1';
SELECT CompanyName FROM Suppliers WHERE Country = 'Germany';

SELECT c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName, COUNT(p.ProductID) AS ProductCount FROM Categories c JOIN Products p ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName ORDER BY ProductCount DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT strftime('%Y', OrderDate) AS Year, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount FROM Orders GROUP BY Year ORDER BY Year;
SELECT s.CompanyName AS ShipperName, ROUND(AVG(o.Freight), 2) AS AvgFreight FROM Orders o JOIN Shippers s ON o.ShipVia = s.ShipperID GROUP BY s.ShipperID, s.CompanyName ORDER BY s.CompanyName
rows.note: Assuming "shipper" means the ShipVia company on each order, I'll group orders by Shippers and average their Freight.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM Employees e WHERE e.ReportsTo = (SELECT EmployeeID FROM Employees WHERE FirstName = 'Andrew' AND LastName = 'Fuller')

WITH counts AS (
  SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, COUNT(*) AS n
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2020'
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeID, FullName
)
SELECT FullName, n AS OrderCount FROM counts WHERE n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM counts);
SELECT COUNT(*) AS ProductCount FROM Products WHERE UnitPrice > (SELECT AVG(UnitPrice) FROM Products);
rows.note: Assuming "average product unit price" is the simple average of UnitPrice across all products in the Products table.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS OrderCount FROM Orders WHERE ShipCountry = 'France';
rows.note: Assuming "shipped to France" means ShipCountry = 'France' in the Orders table, counting all orders regardless of whether ShippedDate is filled in.

rows.sql: SELECT p.ProductName AS product_name, ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS revenue FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.ProductName ORDER BY SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) DESC LIMIT 5
rows.note: Assumption: revenue per line is UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount), summed per product, with the top 5 by that total.

rows.sql:
SELECT c.CategoryName, p.ProductName, p.UnitPrice
FROM Products p
JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID
WHERE p.UnitPrice = (
  SELECT MAX(p2.UnitPrice) FROM Products p2 WHERE p2.CategoryID = p.CategoryID
)
ORDER BY c.CategoryName;

SELECT c.CompanyName, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS Revenue
FROM Orders o
JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
JOIN Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2021'
GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName
HAVING SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) = (
  SELECT MAX(t.Rev) FROM (
    SELECT SUM(od2.UnitPrice * od2.Quantity * (1 - od2.Discount)) AS Rev
    FROM Orders o2
    JOIN "Order Details" od2 ON od2.OrderID = o2.OrderID
    WHERE strftime('%Y', o2.OrderDate) = '2021'
    GROUP BY o2.CustomerID
  ) t
);

SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS MonthNumber, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount FROM Orders WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2021' GROUP BY MonthNumber HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM Orders WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2021' GROUP BY strftime('%m', OrderDate)))
rows.note: I'll count orders by calendar month of `OrderDate` for 2021 and return the top month, keeping any ties.

rows.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID
  WHERE o.OrderDate >= '1997-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '1998-01-01'
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName
)
SELECT EmployeeID, FirstName, LastName, OrderCount
FROM counts
WHERE OrderCount = (SELECT MAX(OrderCount) FROM counts);
rows.note: The Orders table has no orders dated in 1997. It covers only 2012 through 2023, so no employee can be identified for 1997.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS late_shipped_orders FROM Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL AND ShippedDate > RequiredDate;
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped after required date" means ShippedDate is not null and ShippedDate > RequiredDate.

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(ShippedDate) - julianday(OrderDate)), 1) AS avg_days_to_ship FROM Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL;
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped orders" means orders with a non-null ShippedDate, and the day count uses julianday differences.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM Products WHERE Discontinued = '0' AND UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel

SELECT c.Country, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount FROM Orders o JOIN Customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2019-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2020-01-01' GROUP BY c.Country ORDER BY OrderCount DESC LIMIT 1

SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN c.CategoryName = 'Beverages' THEN od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END) / SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 1) AS BeveragesPct FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2023';

SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_with_all_12_months
FROM (
  SELECT CustomerID
  FROM Orders
  WHERE OrderDate >= '2020-01-01' AND OrderDate < '2021-01-01'
  GROUP BY CustomerID
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%m', OrderDate)) = 12
) t;

WITH order_totals AS (
  SELECT o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS order_value
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID
),
emp_avg AS (
  SELECT EmployeeID, AVG(order_value) AS avg_order_value
  FROM order_totals
  GROUP BY EmployeeID
)
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS full_name, ea.avg_order_value
FROM emp_avg ea
JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = ea.EmployeeID
WHERE ea.avg_order_value = (SELECT MAX(avg_order_value) FROM emp_avg);

SELECT s.CompanyName, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS Revenue FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID JOIN Suppliers s ON s.SupplierID = p.SupplierID WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2018-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2019-01-01' GROUP BY s.SupplierID, s.CompanyName ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1
